title: Flow Trigger Design
opening: Choose conditions that seem to help you work on a real task. Then compare the work and how the session felt; absorption alone cannot show that the work improved.

labels.conditionsText: Start from your own practice log or other observations: list recurring place, time, social, preparation, challenge, goal-clarity and feedback conditions. M023 Flow State Analysis can help, but you do not need to complete it first. Use a question from work you actually need to explain; if none is at hand, use: “How does a familiar process work?” Write a short answer, then set the conditions you want to examine.
labels.conversation: Explain it while someone asks questions
labels.question: Write one question before starting
labels.newTask: Explain it for a new reader
labels.clarityCheck: Ask the reader to restate it
labels.personCheck: Ask the reader what is still unclear
labels.draftPrompt: Write two or three sentences that answer the task question.
labels.draftPlaceholder: Your answer to the reader’s question…
labels.plannedSession: What this arrangement asks you to do
labels.quietGoal: Answer the reader’s question in a short explanation.
labels.conversationGoal: Explain the process aloud and answer one follow-up question.
labels.quietGoal: Answer the reader’s question in a short explanation.
labels.conversationGoal: Explain the process aloud and answer one follow-up question.
labels.prepWithQuestion: Before drafting, write the reader’s question: “How does this process work?”
labels.prepWithoutQuestion: Start from the task without writing a reader question first.
labels.sameChallenge: Explain the same process for the same reader.
labels.newChallenge: Explain the same process to a new reader who needs one extra detail.
labels.noCheckEvidence: After drafting, keep the answer as evidence. Its clarity has not been checked by a reader.
labels.clarityCheckEvidence: Ask the reader to restate the answer in their own words. Compare their restatement with the task question; record what matched and what was missing.
labels.personCheckEvidence: Ask the reader which part remains unclear. Record their words and revise only after you have noted the original answer.
labels.comparisonText: Think of an earlier attempt at a similar task where this condition was absent. Compare the actual writing and how absorbed you felt. If the task or other conditions differed, note them; if no useful earlier attempt exists, record that and use this attempt as your first observation.
labels.engagementEvidence: Engagement: how absorbed or distracted you felt.
labels.disruptionEvidence: Disruption: interruptions or other conditions that broke the attempt.
labels.performanceEvidence: Performance: the draft, reader response and what the answer enabled the reader to explain.
labels.unknownEvidence: Unknown: which condition, if any, made a difference when other things also changed.
labels.plan: Record what happened and choose the next adjustment

feedback.unavailable: Saving is unavailable here. Your plan remains on screen.
feedback.missing: Complete the task goal, a baseline, a comparison plan, separate outcome notes and a revision before saving.
feedback.readFailure: Your saved plan could not be loaded. Your current answers remain here.
feedback.conflict: This plan changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here. Save again to keep these answers.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same answers before changing them.

practice.prediction: What task are you arranging? What should the reader be able to explain after reading your answer?
practice.observation: What did an actual earlier attempt show about engagement, disruption and how clearly your answer worked? If none exists, say what you will observe first.
practice.comparison: Which one condition will you examine? What real attempt can you compare with where it was absent? Record other differences or say when you do not know.
practice.result: After the attempt, how absorbed were you, what disrupted the work, and what did the draft or reader response show? Keep these separate.
practice.revision: What difficulty repeated, or what did the reader still need? How could you adjust the task challenge to fit your current ability?
practice.step: What will you change next time? How will you compare that attempt with a real session where the condition was absent?

source.relatedEvidence: M023 Flow State Analysis is an evidence reference; it is not a required lesson prerequisite.
